title: Long run debrief with Jordan
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). After a Saturday sixteen-kilometer long run, Alex and Jordan go over Alex's pacing, the knee and strength work, recovery with sleep and the new running playlist, and a race plan for the half marathon.

utterances.text: Sixteen k! Your longest run ever. How do you feel?
Like a folding chair someone sat on wrong. But happy.
Okay, debrief. Your first three k were way too fast. I saw your watch, you were under five thirty.
I know. I felt amazing and I thought, maybe I'm just fast now.
Everyone thinks that at kilometer two. Then kilometer twelve shows up.
Kilometer twelve was a disaster. I was basically walking up that hill by the marina.
Right. The plan said six fifteen per kilometer. Boring is the point.
So start slower than feels right.
Way slower. If the first half feels too easy, you're doing it right.
Also, can we talk about the goose?
No.
It chased you, Jordan. Hissing. For like fifty meters.
It was guarding its babies. I respect that goose.
You screamed higher than the goose. Anyway, good news, the knee was fine.
Wait, really? The whole sixteen?

The whole way. A little tight at the end, but no sharp pain. The strength work is actually working. Step-downs and glute bridges, twice a week since you sent the plan. The step-downs are still humiliating.
Keep them in. They're why you're not limping right now.
And I slept better this week. Like seven and a half hours most nights.
That shows. Your easy runs looked easy for once.
Also, the playlist helped. The slow one from after the concert. I didn't sprint every time a song changed.
Did Saltwater come on at the end?
At kilometer fifteen. I almost cried.
Perfect. Okay, race plan. Half marathon is five weeks away.
What's the goal? Just finish?
Finish strong. Run the first ten k at long-run pace, then if you feel good, speed up a little each kilometer.
So the opposite of today.
Exactly the opposite. And practice your race breakfast on the next long run. Nothing new on race day.
Oats, banana, coffee. Same as this morning.
Good. Next Saturday, eighteen k. And we take the long way around the goose.
